function: MATD3 agents (UAVs) learn RIS phase shifts jointly with UAV acceleration (trajectory) and task-offloading amounts to maximize energy efficiency of the RIS-aided UAV relay-MEC system (p. 7)
system: Four 4-antenna UAV relays, single-antenna UEs and AP, passive reflecting 10 x 10 URA RIS on a building, carrier given as 750 MHz (p. 3, 10)
method: Modified MATD3 with centralized twin critics, bounded-activation actors, action-change regularization and an interference penalty in the reward; reinforcement learning (p. 8-9)
data_channel: Custom simulated channels: LoS UAV-RIS and UE-UAV links, Rician UAV-AP and RIS-AP links, path-loss exponents 2.3-3; perfect CSI assumed (p. 3, 4, 10)
test_conditions: Trained in the simulated environment; evaluated over task volume, number of tasks, AP distance, LoS/NLoS and Rician factor; no train/test split or retraining stated (p. 11-12)
baselines: Learned: RIS-based MADDPG, No-RIS MADDPG, original MATD3, DDPG (Table II). Non-learned: CCCP/SCA optimization with predefined RIS (p. 10-13)
metrics: Reward, data reception rate (throughput) versus tasks and distance, energy consumption, task completion rate, latency, interference level, convergence time (p. 11-13)
q1_support: p. 4: "We consider the LoS channel for the" UE-UAV and UAV-RIS links; p. 10: "and the path loss exponents are" set by hand; custom simulated LoS and Rician channels, no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO, or measured data.
q2_support: p. 12: "Table I summarizes the average throughput under different channel conditions"; this is a sweep of performance, and the paper does not say that the policy was trained under other conditions or retrained, so no new-condition test is stated.
q3_support: p. 10: "We employ the CCCP algorithm to optimize" is the non-learned optimization baseline; p. 12: "outperforms the original MATD3, MADDPG, and DDPG" is the comparison with standard DRL on reward, completion rate, energy, and latency (Table II, p. 13).
q4_support: p. 13: "it converges in just 2500 episodes"; only the convergence in episodes is given, and the paper reports no complexity order, FLOPs, parameter count, or runtime of the method.
q5_support: p. 10: "There are four UAVs, one AP, and 50 UEs (randomly generated)"; the data are synthetic, and the paper gives no link, DOI, or release statement for code or data (only pseudo-code in the appendix, p. 13), and uses no public dataset.
notes: Included. Area 6 by the specificity order (aerial relay link, learned RIS phase shifts and resources, p. 7); area 3 (RIS configuration) also fits, so the reviewer may confirm. The above_phy check passes because the learned action holds the RIS phase shifts together with UAV acceleration and offloading amounts (p. 7). The RIS is mounted on a building, not on the UAV (p. 3). The text is inconsistent: 5 UEs (p. 9) versus 50 UEs (p. 10), the carrier is printed as a wavelength of 750 MHz (p. 9), and Table II lists interference of -55 dB for the proposed method against -70 dB for DDPG while the text calls it reduced (p. 12-13). q3 rests on CCCP and on MADDPG and DDPG; the original MATD3 is a variant of the proposed method and is not counted. Page numbers count PDF pages.
